note: Each mode is heard against its parent, then its one colour note is tapped on a tenor staff with the root; three modes, three keys, three listening tasks. Each block says what to press and where the changed note shows.

exercise.title: Modes by their colour note
exercise.focus: G Mixolydian ♭7 · D Dorian 6 · E Phrygian ♭2, over a drone
exercise.why: A mode is easiest to recognise by the one note that differs from plain major or minor.

sections.text: Press Play below. The backing holds a G chord for eight bars: four in G major, then four in G Mixolydian. Follow the notes view and listen for the bar where it changes. The faded note is the one left out: F in the first half, F♯ in the second.
The note that changed is {{b7}} (F). Tap {{1}} on the staff, then {{b7}}, then {{1}} again.
Press Play below. This time it's D natural minor, then D Dorian, over Dm; the note that changes is {{6}} (B).
Tap {{1}} then {{6}} on the staff, then tap up the scale from {{1}}, stopping on {{6}}.

Press Play below to start the drone on E. Phrygian's colour note is {{b2}} (F), a half step above the root. Tap {{1}} {{b2}} {{1}} on the staff against the drone, then tap around the whole scale, coming back to {{b2}} whenever you like.
